# 4.2 Bipartiteness, cycle detection, topological sort

Phase 4 (Graphs), target rating 1600–2000. Bank status: short.

## Patterns

### Two-colouring (`two-colouring`)

Split vertices into two sides with every edge crossing, or report impossible.

**Works because:** A graph can be two-coloured exactly when it has no cycle of odd length.

### Cycles in directed graphs (`directed-cycle`)

Detect a directed cycle, or output one, using vertex states (unvisited, on stack, finished).

**Works because:** A directed graph has a cycle exactly when a depth-first traversal meets an edge to a vertex still on the stack.

### Order respecting dependencies (`dependency-order`)

Order tasks so every prerequisite comes first, or report that it is impossible.

**Works because:** The dependency graph has no directed cycle.

### Lexicographically smallest order (`smallest-order`)

Among valid dependency orders, output the lexicographically smallest one, using a min-heap of available vertices.

**Works because:** The graph has no directed cycle, and taking the smallest available vertex never blocks a smaller choice later.

### Cycles in undirected graphs (`undirected-cycle`)

Detect or output a cycle in an undirected graph from a non-tree edge of a traversal.

**Works because:** An undirected graph has a cycle exactly when a traversal meets an already visited vertex other than its parent.
